card.title: Biotechnological applications in agriculture: Bt cotton, …

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Bt cotton makes Cry protein from bacterial cry genes, especially cryIAc and cryIIAb. The protein kills susceptible bollworms only after their alkaline gut activates it, and a non-Bt refuge slows resistance. Nematode-resistant tobacco instead uses RNA interference so Meloidogyne incognita silences one of its own essential genes when it feeds.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Bt path: cry gene in the plant → Cry crystal protein → alkaline gut → active toxin → midgut pores.
RNAi path: plant dsRNA matching a nematode gene → nematode eats it → nematode mRNA silenced.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Bt cotton is not protected only by spraying the live bacterium on the leaves. The cry gene is inside the plant.  ·  Cry protein does not kill every insect that visits the field. Activation needs a susceptible gut.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Spell Bacillus thuringiensis once, then Bt is enough.  ·  cryIAc and cryIIAb are the cotton pair. Do not replace them with a random cry name.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A bollworm larva eating Bt cotton ingests Cry protein and dies after its midgut is damaged.  ·  A honeybee collecting nectar, and not chewing the bollworm's leaf tissue, is not the organism the cry gene was built to kill.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The tobacco method does not put a Cry toxin into the nematode. It silences a nematode gene with RNA.  ·  A refuge is not wasted land. It is the part of the plan that slows resistance.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Compare Bt cotton and RNAi tobacco in a two-column answer.  ·  Explain resistance and the refuge in three sentences.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Bt = protein. Tobacco nematode = RNAi.  ·  Inactive crystal in the bacterium. Active toxin only in the larva.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Why is the Cry protein harmless as a crystal inside the bacterium?  ·  Which nematode is the tobacco example aimed at, and how does the plant stop it?

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Name Bacillus thuringiensis and the alkaline gut. Both are required for a full Bt answer.  ·  For the tobacco question, write Meloidogyne incognita and RNA interference. Do not answer it with Cry protein.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: cryIAc and cryIIAb  ·  Alkaline-gut activation  ·  Refuge strategy  ·  Meloidogyne incognita

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Source of cry: Bacillus thuringiensis.  ·  Activation: alkaline insect gut → pores in the midgut.  ·  Cotton genes named in the course: cryIAc and cryIIAb.  ·  Refuge of non-Bt plants slows resistance.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bacillus thuringiensis produces insecticidal crystal proteins during sporulation.  ·  RNA interference destroys or blocks an mRNA that matches the introduced double-stranded RNA.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Why would planting only Bt cotton for many years weaken the method?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A root-knot nematode on the modified tobacco fails to establish because a gene it needs has been silenced.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The cry genes in Bt cotton come from → B  ·  Cry protein becomes an active toxin in → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Bt cotton carries cry genes from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis. The plant makes the Cry protein in its own tissues. Bollworm larvae that eat the leaf or the boll take the protein in with the meal.  ·  Inside the bacterium the Cry protein is an inactive crystal. In the alkaline gut of a susceptible larva it dissolves and is cut into an active toxin. The toxin forms pores in the midgut lining and the larva dies. cryIAc and cryIIAb are the genes used against cotton bollworms.  ·  The toxin is not a general insect killer. It needs that alkaline gut. Pollinators that do not eat the tissue, and insects whose guts do not activate the crystal, are not the target. The human stomach is acidic, and people do not have the insect midgut receptor the toxin uses.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: RNA interference versus Cry protein  ·  Tobacco RNAi targets Meloidogyne incognita, a root-knot nematode.  ·  The refuge figure used in teaching is at least about 20 percent non-Bt plants.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Agrobacterium is the delivery tool for the RNAi construct, not the pest.  ·  The crystal protein is inactive until the insect gut processes it.  ·  Bt is a protein toxin. The nematode defence is RNA silencing.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Continuous exposure without a refuge favours resistant insects.  ·  Write the Bt path from gene to dead larva in four steps.  ·  Explain what a non-Bt refuge is for.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Contrast the molecule that protects Bt cotton with the molecule that protects the tobacco.  ·  A field of only Bt plants selects for larvae that survive the toxin. A refuge of non-Bt cotton, about a fifth of the area, lets susceptible insects survive and mate with resistant survivors. That mating dilutes resistance.  ·  Nematode-resistant tobacco uses RNA interference against the root-knot nematode Meloidogyne incognita. Agrobacterium is used to put into the plant a DNA sequence that produces double-stranded RNA matching a gene the nematode needs.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: When the nematode feeds on the root it takes up that RNA. The matching mRNA in the worm is silenced, so the nematode cannot develop properly in the root. The protection is gene silencing, not a protein crystal. Bt and this RNAi crop solve pest problems by different molecules.  ·  # Biotechnological applications in agriculture: Bt cotton, nematode-resistant tobacco ## 1.
